2.cardLine: Short moves ease stiffness and nudge alertness.
2.detail: Research on active microbreaks suggests ~2–3 minutes of light movement can ease desk discomfort and help you stay sharper than sitting locked in one pose. Tiny resets also stack — how often you break up sitting matters, not just gym minutes.
2.doneLine: Two minutes well spent. Your joints just got a meeting break.

5.cardLine: Open hips and chest; wake energy mid-day.
5.detail: Five minutes is enough to undo the laptop shape — hips, chest, upper back — and light standing work helps circulation after a sit block. Active breaks are also linked with less perceived fatigue than unbroken desk time.
5.doneLine: Midday unkink complete. Blood moved. Brain slightly less mush.

10.cardLine: Full desk-chain reset after a heavy sit day.
10.detail: A longer circuit hits neck to calves in one pass — a real sit-interrupt, not just a stretch snack. Breaking up long sitting with light movement is studied for comfort and for how the body handles a sedentary day; breathe out slow at the end to leave work mode calmer.
10.doneLine: Full-stack cleanup done. The chair can have you back — briefly.

benefitBlurbs.title: Ease desk stiffness
benefitBlurbs.body: Short active microbreaks (about 2–3 minutes of light movement) are linked with less perceived musculoskeletal discomfort versus staying locked in one posture.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Changing joint angles and lightly loading muscles reduces continuous tissue strain from static sitting.

benefitBlurbs.title: Protect alertness
benefitBlurbs.body: Breaking long sits with brief light activity helps counter the dip in how awake and sharp people feel during unbroken desk work.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Posture change + light muscle work; related research on walking breaks shows they can help maintain cerebral blood flow that otherwise drifts down with prolonged sitting.

benefitBlurbs.title: Feasible every meeting gap
benefitBlurbs.body: Tiny resets are easier to repeat than a workout — and frequency of sit-breaks matters as much as total exercise minutes for many desk-day effects.
benefitBlurbs.mechanism: Habit stacking: short bouts accumulate across the day without needing a gym or outfit change.

steps.positionCue: Stand tall. Slide your chin straight back (soft double chin). Eyes level — don’t tip the nose down.
Stand with soft knees. Inhale through the nose, then sigh out through the mouth longer than the inhale. Soft shoulders.
